summary: Wilkes County tower on a 2016 tnlandforms list with coordinates, elevation and an older GFC number; no history, staffing or site status found.

evidence.supports: Tignall record: Wilkes County, coordinates, 642 ft, older GFC number 011
The list was last revised in March 2016
The gfc-nnn numbers come from an older GFC list that described 203 towers
evidence.quote: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers (gfc-nnn).

evidence.supports: Names for towers numbered 73 and above are the page author's own
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

evidence.supports: Staffing on the state's towers has been cut steadily since the late 1980s
evidence.quote: Since the late 1980s, the state has steadily cut its fire tower staff

evidence.supports: In 1987 the state staffed 93 towers full time and 73 seasonally
evidence.quote: in 1987, the state staffed 93 towers full time and 73 seasonally

evidence.supports: 2006 spreadsheet: 137 of 144 still-existing towers no longer staffed
evidence.quote: 137 of the state's 144 still-existing towers are no longer staffed.

evidence.supports: Towers being auctioned off, some sold for scrap metal
evidence.quote: The towers are being auctioned off - sold for scrap metal in some cases

sources.title: Fire towers are fading into history

notes_for_editor: The list gives elevation with no unit; the story reads it as feet.Only one 2016 list supports this record. No source found for build date, status, access, staffing, height, design or photos, so none is set. Agency is not set: the list shows GFC numbers, not ownership. The name is the list author's label, not a documented name. The Savannah Now article is read from a Wayback Machine copy because the live site returned 403; it is used for statewide context only. The NHLR Georgia list (29 registered lookouts) does not name this tower, and the FFLOS Georgia list has only two sites (Lafayette, Yonah Mountain). GFC history page timed out and was not used.
